Sam (AE): Quick check-in: Ravi's infra team needs the on-prem POC to stay on a locked image for the pilot (6-9 months). No automatic callbacks allowed. They also want a documented emergency hotfix delivery mechanism. Thoughts?
Priya (SE): That's a common ask. We can support image freezes + signed hotfix bundles delivered out-of-band, but we need an agreed process for signing, verification, and chain-of-custody.
Ravi (Customer): Exactly. We can't have any network egress from the POC cluster. Delivery will be via a customer-controlled jumpbox or physical media. We need the process spelled out for our auditors.
Ana (Legal): From contract perspective we'll need scoped obligations for hotfixes (SLA, number of hotfixes covered, liability). We'll also need acceptance criteria for what qualifies as a "critical" fix.
Priya (SE): Operational points: 1) We produce a signed delta or full bundle (tar.gz) + signed manifest. 2) Customer verifies signature and checksum. 3) We provide installation steps and rollback commands. Example verification: `gpg --verify manifest.sig manifest.json && sha256sum -c manifest.json`
Sam (AE): Commercially, we should price for manual build/sign/deliver work. Suggest a fixed monthly retainer for freeze support + per-hotfix fee.
Ana (Legal): Also require an attestation that the delivered artifact was signed with our Notary key. That reduces non-repudiation risk. We should provide exported cert chain for audit.
Ravi (Customer): 48-72h SLA for critical hotfixes is preferred. We can accept 72h if it's well-documented and there's a war-room channel.
Priya (SE): 72h is reasonable if we pre-stage build artifacts and have signing ops oncall. For 48h we'd need a dedicated oncall rotation.
Sam (AE): Which option does the team prefer? 48h paid fast-track or 72h standard included in SOW?
Ravi (Customer): We'll aim for 72h. If we hit a live exploit we'll negotiate escalation.
Priya (SE): Tech constraints to note for the runbook: - If model weights change we may need a full-image rebuild. - GPU driver updates can't be backported; freeze implies we lock tested driver/kernel combo. - Transitive OS package CVEs might require broader rebuilds.
Sam (AE): Understood. We'll document compatibility matrix and a lockfile indicating approved OS/kernel/runtime versions.
Ana (Legal): Also include export controls language if media crosses borders. Chain-of-custody forms should include signer, timestamp, hash, and delivery method.
Priya (SE): Runbook minimum deliverables: signed manifest, signed bundle, install script, verify commands, rollback script, and a short security bulletin describing the fix.
Ravi (Customer): For delivery channels we prefer: 1) scp to a customer jumpbox (preferred), 2) USB with tamper-evident seal, 3) couriered disk (last resort). We'll accept GPG or Notary v2 signatures.
Priya (SE): We'll do Notary v2 signatures and include a GPG fallback. For USB delivery add an MD5/sha256 printed on the packing slip.
Sam (AE): Action items: Priya to draft the technical runbook + manifest template; Ana to draft SOW clause and acceptance language; Sam to propose pricing uplift and retainer model. I'll set a PS kickoff when SOW signs.
deliver-bot: Ticket POC-8392 created for "onprem-freeze-hotfix-process".
Ravi (Customer): I'll loop in our sec-ops (secops@ravi-inc.com) and procurement. Expect confirmation by COB Fri.
Priya (SE): I'll post the initial runbook draft here tomorrow.
Sam (AE): Thanks everyone. Keeping thread for the audit trail.
